items.title: Higgsfield launches playable game ads built with AI
items.excerpt: Higgsfield launched an enterprise-only playable-ads workflow: developers describe a mechanic, pick genre and dimension, upload up to 100 sprites/textures/SFX and generate an exportable HTML playable ad for AppLovin, Meta, Google or TikTok. Its playable-games tool can also be driven from Claude via Higgsfield MCP.

items.title: Sony patents AI that plays your game while you eat dinner
items.excerpt: A newly publicized Sony patent splits a game into play units (quests, missions, scenes) and trains a separate AI helper per unit from real players' runs; the console shows which parts the AI can take over and the player can grab the controller back anytime. Distinct from Sony's earlier 'ghost player' filing.

items.title: Unreal Engine 5.9 Preview 2 Brings Browser-Based Gaming To Blueprint-Only Projects, Enables AI Workflows By Default And Improves Rendering
items.excerpt: Epic's new UE 5.9 Preview 2 build turns on the default AI toolsets, adds Blueprint-only web game export with WebGPU improvements, and speeds up cinematic workflows - a new build, not a recap of the UE6 Blueprints announcement.

items.title: Slotbound: a 200,000-copy Steam hit built with AI coding tools by a near-zero-experience solo developer
items.excerpt: Solo developer Optima Arch, with almost no prior programming or game-dev experience, built the slot-roguelike Slotbound over about eight months using AI coding tools, then hand-tuned systems, balance and UI. It sold 100,000 copies in three days and passed 200,000 in six days on Steam.

items.title: Clash Royale recruits creator of AI cheating tool to help catch cheaters
items.excerpt: Supercell said the creator of an advanced AI cheating tool for Clash Royale was caught and has agreed to join the team building new anti-cheat technology, a day after warning that AI cheating would get players banished from the Arena.

items.title: Chess.com's next move is a new hub for classic games, from mahjong to sudoku
items.excerpt: Chess.com launched Classic, a hub of classic games from mahjong to sudoku, built by a very small team using AI mainly to speed up coding on top of its existing code base, design system and bot characters; the company says AI was not used for the games' art and design.

items.title: One way to stave off AI clones? Minimise the gap between announcement and launch
items.excerpt: Tinybuild's Alex Nichiporchik explains how a three-month reveal-to-release window for Probably Stolen was a defence against generative-AI copycats that reverse-engineer demos, as studios rethink the 'announce early, build wishlists' playbook.

items.title: Steam games that disclose AI use tend to sell less - but is the disclosure really the cause?
items.excerpt: A statistical report estimating Steam sales from review counts found titles with AI-use disclosures sell less overall; AUTOMATON's read is that many disclosed titles were set up to lose from the start rather than being hurt by the label itself.

items.title: Wrtn on 'hyper-personalization' and the future of AI entertainment beyond novel/manga/game categories [G-STAR 2026]
items.excerpt: At the G-CON 2026 main session, Wrtn (maker of the AI character app Crack, G-STAR's main sponsor) argued AI is collapsing content-production cost and branching experiences per user, blurring the line between novels, comics and games into a 'Narrative Industry'.

items.title: [AI & LAW] 지스타 간판 된 AI 게임…국내는 '설계' 심의, EU는 '결함' 묻는다
items.excerpt: With Wrtn's AI chatbot Crack as G-STAR's first non-game main sponsor, Korea's Game Rating and Administration Committee says AI chat alone is not a game but paid-currency probability mechanics can be; a new youth-protection bill would review 'relational AI services' by their design, while the EU moves to post-hoc liability.

items.title: Genie 4 is now available on the Gemini API
items.excerpt: Google opened the Genie 4 world model to developers through the Gemini API, letting them build interactive 720p worlds with native audio and real-time controls; reports put pricing at roughly $0.10 per second of streamed world. Distinct from the earlier AI Ultra consumer rollout.

items.title: AI Evaluates, Humans Decide: The Next Step in Game Rating Classification
items.excerpt: A Nexon-led industry-academic consortium presented first-year results and plans for AI-assisted game rating technology, in which AI pre-evaluates game content and human reviewers make the final classification decision.

items.title: Imitation Disputes Shift from 'Like Games' to 'AI Cloning'
items.excerpt: Korean legal experts say the focus of game imitation disputes is moving from genre/rule-copying 'like games' to AI cloning, where AI is used to replicate games in their entirety.

items.title: Legal Experts Re-examine 'Boundaries of Games' Surrounding AI Chat Apps and Private Server Users
items.excerpt: On November 20, legal and academic experts examined how AI character-chat apps and illegal private servers are challenging where Korean game regulation draws the line on what counts as a game.

items.title: Unity and AI: What to vibe code and where to rely on infrastructure
items.excerpt: Unity's guidance on where AI-assisted 'vibe coding' with the Unity CLI pays off (prototypes, UI) and where teams should rely on managed Unity infrastructure for CAD pipelines, security and scale.

items.title: Introducing Voice Isolator
items.excerpt: Inworld released Voice Isolator, two 48 kHz models (offline and realtime streaming) that strip background noise while keeping speech, laughter and breaths, with code and weights under Apache 2.0 - a separate release from its SAVA launch.
